quiz_map.support: The identity log sees a connected app that never crosses the gateway at all, because the AI service reads the mailbox from its own servers.
A request of several megabytes is a file, or a very long paste.
Match on the registered domain, or on an exact list of names, never on a substring.
On its own, marking an app Unsanctioned does not block it.
The same domain where the process is anything else is an installed client or a script.
A value of Principal means an individual user consented for data related only to that account.
The gateway adds an HTTP header to every request to the service, naming the organisations or workspaces that are allowed.
The grant lets the supplier read every file r.hale can reach, at any time.
a POST with data to a host that is not the sanctioned tool
Upload volume is the request size, not the response size.
Finance, HR (human resources) and Legal handle the data that hurts most when it leaves.
When a rule catches exactly the behaviour it was written for and the activity is authorised, the verdict is benign true positive, not false positive.
ConsentType Principal means one user consented for data related only to that account.
To stop a connected app, disable it instead of deleting it: a deleted app can return when the next user consents.
The fix is a tenant restriction: the gateway inserts an HTTP header naming the allowed organisation, and the service refuses every other account.
Extensions make few connections of their own, so you find them in the extension inventory, not in network logs.
A substring rule fires on any unrelated domain that happens to contain the same letters.
Attribution comes before assessment because you cannot judge a tool's risk without knowing who uses it and what they send.
If people relied on the tool, pair the block with an approved replacement.
Upload volume is the request size, not the response size.
